I'm pretty sure this has been posted before, but I do agree that it's a good idea. I would recommend only making posts movable to /v/whatever, since moving a post to another subverse has a few problems:

  • the destination sub might not be the right place for a post either, and we'd end up playing a game of hot potato
  • anyone can make a sub and then troll other subs by transplanting popular posts that go against the spirit of the destination sub
  • the main issue is that preserving upvoats would mean large subs would have an instant #1 post in smaller subs, and transplanting a post directly into another sub's front page is easily abused

Moving posts to /v/whatever mitigates all of these downsides and still allows mods to relocate an off-topic post without killing an ongoing discussion. It feels to me like the perfect complement to the mod log.

This is a good idea but there are some issues that could arise from this. Allowing a mod to move a post to another subverse without some form of protection for the other subverses would allow abuse to run rampant. Instead of moving a post to another subverse, hide the post and include the proper subverse link in a message to the user like, "Your post has been hidden because it is off-topic and would be better suited for [insert sub link here]. If you have any guestions regarding this then contact the mods of this subverse." It's simple, points the user to the proper subverse and keeps discussions on-topic. It's a win-win-win.

Technically hiding the post is what happens now. Deleted posts no longer show in a subverse, but are present in the modlog and ongoing discussion can still continue there. Moving a post to /v/whatever would be an alternative for things that break subverse rules by being off topic for that sub. It would have to also be logged, of course, so I'm sure there are more details to work out than what we're thinking of here.

It has to do with both your nose and oxidation. Your nose has two sets of nerves in it. One set is active when you breath in through your nose. The other set is active when you breath out. This is why some people love stinky cheese. It is only stinky when in is outside the mouth. As soon as it is in the mouth and you are pulling air over it and exhausting that air out of your nose and across the second set of olfactory nerves, the cheese doesn't smell bad.

The second set of nerves also responds to the oxidizing molecules in teas. When the tea is hot, just after steeping, one sips it in short bursts. This usually results in low oxidized molecules being pulled off the top of the tea and exhausted out the nose- and (if its a quality tea with few pesticides) activates the second set of nerves in a pleasurable manner.

As tea sits after steeping, it rapidly oxidizes. You can see this in the gradual darkening of its color. The longer it sits, the cooler it gets, you drink bigger sips, the brain focuses on the taste buds, the brain registers fewer responses from olfactory nerves, and the more the tea's flavor deteriorates.

Ice Tea has sugar or lemon in it to mask the oxidized tea molecules.
